steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR): drafted in 1950, ratified by the UK in 1951. Protects fundamental rights: right to life (Article 2), prohibition of torture (Article 3), right to liberty (Article 5), right to a fair trial (Article 6), right to privacy (Article 8), freedom of expression (Article 10), freedom of assembly (Article 11), and right to marry (Article 12). | Key Fact: The Human Rights Act 1998: incorporated ECHR rights into UK law. UK courts can now hear human rights cases without going to Strasbourg. Courts can declare legislation 'incompatible' with the ECHR (but cannot strike it down - Parliament decides). Public authorities (including the government, police, councils) must act compatibly with ECHR rights. | Key Fact: Key rights explained: Right to life
